C028.notes: SER EU-MT-003. Mnajdra Temple altar/trilithon · MALTA · 2013 · 12 EU stars. Country #9. Joseph ~25% Maltese (father’s father). Temple complex ~3600–3200 BC — some of the oldest free-standing stone architecture on Earth, now riding a five-cent piece in a cardboard flip. Heritage coin. Keep forever energy. SER siblings: EU-MT-001 · EU-MT-002. Malta flips now 3.

open_questions: Type catalogued KM#128 for Malta 5 euro cent, but Numista and Colnect list the Malta 5c as KM#127 (KM#128 is the 10c). All three Malta euro types in the collection appear shifted +1 - verify the whole set.

C028.story: A 2013 Maltese 5-euro-cent coin. Malta's side shows the altar stone of the prehistoric Mnajdra temple, with the word MALTA. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in copper-plated steel.

C043.notes: SER EU-MT-002. Arms of Malta (flag shield · mural crown · olive & palm) · MALTA · 2008 · 12 EU stars. First calendar year of Maltese euro cash. Heritage flag with C028 / EU-MT-003 2013 5€c · C064 / EU-MT-001 €1 Cross. Malta flips now 3.

open_questions: Type catalogued KM#129 for Malta 10 euro cent, but NGC's price guide titles the Malta 10c as KM#128. Same +1 shift seen on the other Malta euro types - verify.

C043.story: A 2008 Maltese 10-euro-cent coin. Malta's side shows the national coat of arms (a shield of the Maltese flag under a crown, with olive and palm branches) and the word MALTA. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

issue.mint_text: Malta (first calendar year of Maltese euro cash; often Paris/Utrecht contract)

Heritage flag with C028 / EU-MT-003 (2013 5€c) and C043 / EU-MT-002 (2008 10€c) — Joseph ~25% Maltese (father’s father) · Hypogeum 2015. First-year euro for the islands. Vault 1000. Malta flips now 3.

open_questions: Type catalogued KM#132 for Malta 1 euro, but Numista lists the Malta 1 euro as KM#131. Same +1 shift seen on the other Malta euro types - verify.

C064.story: A 2008 Maltese 1-euro coin. Malta's side shows the eight-pointed Maltese Cross, designed by Noel Galea Bason. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. It is made of two metals: a copper-nickel center inside a nickel-brass ring.
